key_insight: Spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP) turn symmetry-induced rank constraints in equivariant representations into orientation-invariant measures of structural symmetry and symmetry breaking.
engineering_relevance: SymFP offers a reusable tool for identifying point-group symmetry and tracking local structural changes in materials and molecular systems.
method: Compute singular-value spectra of equivariant representations, with a parameter-free GNN implementation.
Identify discrete point groups by matching spectra to symmetry-specific rank templates.
Quantify continuous symmetry breaking using spectral energy beyond target rank constraints.
evidence_signal: Evaluations span synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, demonstrating point-group identification and sensitivity to controlled, local and degree-resolved symmetry changes.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify robustness to noisy coordinates or numerical thresholds used in rank-template matching.
paper_title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
